hypothesis_update: lower_compose violates its documented error contract on at least one axis: (1) ComposeItem::Internal with an unknown alias or unknown action name is silently accepted (no validation exists in the visible body; the internal set only gates action export), and (2) sync arity mismatches may be downgraded to warnings via &mut warnings rather than returned as CoreError; sync-alias-boundary is needed to confirm which checks exist and their error-vs-warning classification. Secondary candidate defect: ActionItem::Let never inserts its name into the bound set (unlike ForAll binders in rewrite_statement), so let-bound names colliding with component state/consts would be wrongly alias-prefixed in subsequent action items.
rationale: The documented contract promises CoreError for 'unknown aliases or actions, sync arity mismatches', but the full lower_compose body shows it performs no such validation itself: the internal set built from ComposeItem::Internal (lines 291-298) is only used to suppress public action export, so Internal entries naming a missing alias or action are silently ignored, and all remaining validation must live in the callees. sync_action(action, &components, &mut warnings)? is the only callee positioned to implement the alias/arity checks, and the &mut warnings parameter is a red flag that mismatches may be demoted to warnings instead of returned as CoreError, contradicting the contract. This card is named for exactly that boundary and decides whether the function upholds its stated error behavior or hides contract violations behind warnings/absence of checks.
